answer.generated: "Invariance to translation" in the context of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) illustrates how shared weights in a CNN architecture enable the model to recognize features regardless of their position within an input image. This property is visually represented in the image associated with Goodfellow, 2016, where identical weights (denoted as \( w1, w2, w3 \)) are applied across different parts of the input image. As a result, the CNN can detect the same feature regardless of its location, making it robust to translations within the image. This mechanism significantly reduces the complexity of the model by avoiding the need to learn separate filters for every possible position of the same feature.
